title: The hydrosphere

draft.title: The hydrosphere
card: The hydrosphere is all the water on Earth. It includes oceans, rivers, lakes, ice, groundwater and water vapour in the air.
Most of Earth's water is salt water in the oceans. Only a small share is fresh water, and much of that is frozen in ice sheets and glaciers or stored underground as groundwater.
The water cycle moves water between these stores. Heat from the sun evaporates water, the vapour cools and condenses into clouds, and water falls as precipitation.

Water that lands on the ground may run off into rivers, soak in to become groundwater, or freeze as ice. Water in the hydrosphere is always moving, though it moves quickly in some stores and very slowly in others.
draft.remember: The hydrosphere is all of Earth's water in every form, kept moving by the water cycle.

a.q: Which description best fits the hydrosphere?
opts: All of Earth's water in its liquid, solid and gas forms
Only the liquid water found in the oceans and seas
Only the fresh water that people can drink
The layer of gases that holds clouds and rain
a.why: The hydrosphere covers water in every form and place, including ice and water vapour. Oceans are its largest store, but they are not all of it.
a.clue: Think about every place water is found, not just one.

b.q: Rain falls on farmland near Wagga Wagga. Some of it soaks into the soil and fills the spaces between underground rock. Which part of the hydrosphere has the water now joined?
b.why: Water that soaks into the ground and is stored in underground rock is groundwater. It is still part of the hydrosphere, and it can later flow back to rivers or be taken up and evaporated.
b.clue: Where is the water stored once it is underground?

a.best: All of Earth's water in its liquid, solid and gas forms
